'''Patrick John Burke''' (born December 14, 1973) is an Irish former professional [[basketball]] player who is currently the men's basketball head coach for [[Beacon College]]. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for three seasons between 2002 and 2007, for the [[Orlando Magic]] and the [[Phoenix Suns]]. To date, he is the only Irishman to have played in the [[NBA]]. He also played in Europe, mainly in Greece and Spain, before ending his career with [[Asseco Prokom Sopot]]. He was a co-captain of the senior [[Ireland national basketball team|Ireland national team]] and also represented his country at the [[World University Games]].

== Early life ==
Burke was born in [[Dublin]], Ireland.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ireland |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/4948/tid/305/_/2007_EuroBasket/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=27 January 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218134233/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/4948/tid/305/_/2007_EuroBasket/index.html |archive-date=18 December 2019}}</ref> Burke and his family moved from [[Tullamore]] in Ireland, to [[Cleveland, Ohio]] in the United States when he was three years old.<ref>[http://www.britball.com/features/patburke0309.html Dublin boy Burke waits journey's next stop]</ref>

Burke played high school basketball at [[Mariner High School (Cape Coral, Florida)|Mariner High School]] in [[Cape Coral, Florida]]. He played [[college basketball]] at [[Auburn University]] with the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] from 1993 to 1997.

== Professional career ==
=== NBA ===
After not being [[NBA draft|drafted]] out of [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn University]] in 1997, Burke became the first Irish-born player in [[NBA]] history when he signed a contract with the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://m.independent.ie/sport/other-sports/would-it-shock-you-if-i-said-i-dont-watch-the-nba-finals-irelands-only-nba-player-pat-burke/a1101363466.html|title='Would it shock you if I said I don't watch the NBA finals?' – Ireland's only NBA player Pat Burke|date=24 May 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=24 May 2024}}</ref>
He played in 62 games with them, averaging 4.3 points and 2.4 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. He did not play in the NBA during the [[2003–04 NBA season]], or the [[2004–05 NBA season]]. In his return to the NBA, he played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] for two seasons. He was also in training camp with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2007 before being released.

=== Europe ===
Burke was a [[EuroLeague]] champion with [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]] in the 1999–00 season and he also helped the "Greens" to win three consecutive [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] titles from 1999 to 2001. In Europe, he also played with the Spanish clubs [[Tau Ceramica]], [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]] and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], and with [[Maroussi BC|Maroussi]] in Greece. He helped Real to the final of the [[ULEB Cup]] (now called [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]) in 2004 and to the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] title in 2005.

In November 2007, Burke signed with Russian club [[Khimki BC|Khimki]]<ref>[http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2007/november/401/ BC Khimki signed Pat Burke]</ref> and helped the team win their first [[Russian Basketball Cup|Russian Cup]] title. Burke averaged 8.2 points and 5.2 rebounds per game in 211 career games played over all of the different European leagues that he competed in. In 2008, he moved to the Polish club [[Asseco Prokom Sopot]]<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/35864/180 Prokom inks veteran center Burke]</ref> and he helped the team to win [[Polish Basketball League|the league]]'s title.

== Coaching ==
Pat Burke was named the new men's basketball head coach at [[Beacon College]] in [[Leesburg, Florida]] in March 2025. Burke succeeds [[Sam Vincent (basketball)|Sam Vincent]], who coached the Beacon NaviGators/Blazers from 2022 to 2025 and helped the athletic program achieve [[United States Collegiate Athletic Association|USCAA]] membership. Burke has had ties with Beacon College since 2015 when he pitched the idea to begin a summer program at the school for [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] and other international students. He is also the director of athletics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beacon News |date=March 4, 2025 |title=Beacon College Welcomes Pat Burke as Head Men's Basketball Coach and Director of Athletics |url=https://newsouthconference.com/mbb/2025/03/04/beacon-college-welcomes-pat-burke-as-head-mens-basketball-coach-and-director-of-athletics/ |via=newsouthconference.com}}</ref>
